accuracy.note: On fictional test data, 19 Nov 2026. The clean set covers 29 of the 30 agents: every retailer deduction is a decision for a person, so a deduction file with nothing to look at does not exist. These numbers show the rules do what they are written to do on data built to test them, not how they will do on a plant's own exports. This pass also ran two public government files through the agents and fixed three things the injury data showed.

real_data: U.S. Department of Labor, OSHA Injury Tracking Application, Case Detail Data 2024 (Forms 300 and 301)

fairmake-osha-300-log on 5,431 cases from 667 Ohio manufacturing establishments, read in OSHA's own layout: 114 cases with findings (79 day counts over the 180-day cap, 18 missing fields, 13 missing day counts, 5 outcomes that contradict the day counts) and 0 disagreements with an independent re-count of every case. It showed three problems, now fixed: two case numbers that differ only in letter case were merged into one, restriction days on an 'other recordable' case were not caught, and days past 180 were called an error although OSHA lets counting stop there (now listed to watch).

human_review: Whether a variance, price jump or margin loss is real, and every standard, journal, reserve or landed cost posting: the controller decides and posts.
Which BOM, routing, schedule or maintenance change to make, and whether scrap and downtime reasons were recorded right on the floor.
Recounts, stock adjustments, reorder point changes, obsolescence reserves and any hold or recall decision.
Every message to a supplier (expedite, price query, rebate claim, certificate request) and whether to accept the material.
Which deductions to dispute or accept and every corrected ASN or invoice; the trading partner's rules are entered from its guide by a person.
Gauge holds, NCR dispositions and CAPA closure, whether an injury is recordable, and tariff classification with your customs broker.
All of the above: nothing is posted, paid, shipped, filed or sent until a named person on your team clicks.
common_problems: A work order closed with cost charged to it and no finished output.
A receipt priced at 6.00 against a 0.05 standard: a unit-of-measure slip that would inflate inventory value.
Two assemblies whose bills of materials contain each other, so neither can be costed.
A micrometer that failed calibration and was then used on two more work orders.
A safety-critical machine inspection overdue, and a hydraulic oil change past its run hours.
A supplier rebate earned and partly unclaimed after the claim-by date (1,400 of 2,400).
A retailer fine for a late ASN that was sent 2.5 hours after shipping, inside the 24-hour window.
A finished lot built from a bolt lot that was issued before it was received.
reaches_the_model: The checks are plain arithmetic on your computer; no AI model runs inside them. When your assistant calls a tool, its model receives the result: amounts, quantities, dates, rates, finding codes, item and order numbers, supplier and customer names, and free-text fields such as descriptions, scrap and stop reasons as they were typed. Employee, estimator and NCR or CAPA owner names, and job titles in the injury log, are replaced with tokens such as A.R.#3f9a2c (26 planted names, 0 leaks in this pass). Results go to whatever model your assistant uses; for injury records or prices you treat as confidential, use a model covered by your own agreements or a local model. No compliance claim is made.
rules_maintained: Every threshold is a dated setting in your own JSON file, with its default printed in each result as settings_used: cost and price tolerances, aging buckets, scrap standards, reorder review, retailer dispute windows, ASN grace and fines, material specs, tariff codes and duty rates, and the injury log's 180-day cap and 7-day entry window (from OSHA's recordkeeping rule, 29 CFR 1904, as of 19 Nov 2026). You change a setting by editing that file; nothing else needs to change. Rules fixed in code (OSHA's ITA outcome codes, X12 element positions, the named export layouts and column names in nine languages) are maintained by Mythos Machines and change only in a new version; until then a column map in fairmake-sources.json covers a changed export.
